title: Home button tooltip says 'Reset view (center 0,0, FOV 60)' but the action centres on the zenith
what_happened: The command bar's home button is labelled 'Reset view (center 0,0, FOV 60)'. The action it runs (_resetView) deliberately centres on the observer's zenith instead - the code comment says RA 0/Dec 0 'sat 14 deg BELOW the horizon, so reset view pointed the map at the ground'. The tooltip was not updated with the fix.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > hover the house icon in the command bar.
evidence: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/command_bar.dart:78 vs actions.dart:649-658. Observed live: pressing the reset hotkey moved the centre to RA 8h17m31s / Dec +40 00' at LST 08:19 (the zenith), not 0,0 - /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-21.png
verdict_reasoning: command_bar.dart:78 still reads `tooltip: 'Reset view (center 0,0, FOV 60)'` verbatim, while actions.dart:649-658 _resetView reads skyViewHomeCenterProvider (the zenith) and its own comment says RA0/Dec0 'sat 14 deg BELOW the horizon'. I confirmed the behaviour live too: pressing 'h' moved the centre to RA 10h34m45s / Dec +40 00' at LST 10:34, i.e. the zenith, not 0,0. Location is exact.

title: Alt/az readouts ignore precession - stated positions are up to 1.4 degrees off
what_happened: Clicking Capella at 18:38:16Z from 40N/105W/1650m the popup reported Alt 56.5, Az 295.7. Computing alt/az from the same J2000 RA/Dec with no precession gives 56.462/295.700 - an exact match; precessing to the equinox of date gives 56.804/295.681. Pollux at 18:39:17Z: app 76.0/214.0; J2000-direct 75.964/214.167; precessed 76.080/212.716 (1.45 deg of azimuth). So the horizontal transform uses J2000 coordinates unrotated, with no nutation, aberration or refraction either.
expected: Apply precession (and ideally refraction) before the horizontal transform. 26 years from J2000 is already ~22 arcmin of position, and the azimuth error near the zenith reaches 1.4 deg, which is enough to mis-call a meridian-flip or an obstruction check.
repro: Set the site to 40N 105W, open the planetarium at a known UTC, click Capella and Pollux, read 'Current Position'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-22.png (Capella: HYG118360, RA 5h16m40.7s Dec +45 59' 52", Alt 56.5 Az 295.7), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-24.png (Pollux: HIP37826, RA 7h45m17.7s Dec +28 1' 33", Alt 76.0 Az 214.0).
location_wrong: Cited only 'packages/skotiq_planetarium (horizontal transform)'. Precise sites: the transform is equatorialToHorizontal at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:262, and the unused precession routine it should compose with is precessFromJ2000ToDate at the same file :442.
proposed_fix: Precess catalogue J2000 coordinates to the observation epoch before computing hour angle.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own numbers. Clicked Vega at 2026-08-03 20:49:14 UTC from 40N/105W/1650m: popup reports RA 18h36m56.8s / Dec +38 47' 09" (J2000 to the arcsecond) and Alt 6.2 / Az 43.0. Computing alt/az from those unprecessed J2000 coordinates gives 6.2436 / 43.0466 - an exact match; precessing to the equinox of date (rigorous IAU 1976) gives 18h37m50s / +38 48' 36" whose alt/az is 6.1449 / 42.9005, which the app does NOT show. No refraction either - at alt 6.2 deg refraction is ~0.13 deg and the app shows the bare geometric value. Corroborating: AstronomyCalculations.precessFromJ2000ToDate exists at astronomy_calculations.dart:442 but a repo-wide grep finds ZERO call sites - it is dead code.

title: Clicking Capella opens an info popup titled 'HYG118360' while the chart labels the same star 'Capella'
what_happened: The sky draws the label 'Capella'. Clicking it opens the object popup with the heading 'HYG118360', an identifier chip 'HYG118360' and 'mag 1.0'. Capella is V=0.08; the neighbouring Pollux popup correctly shows the proper name 'Pollux', the chip 'HIP37826' and 'mag 1.2' (true 1.14). So for this star the popup contradicts the chart label AND reports a magnitude ~0.9 mag too faint.
expected: The popup heading should use the same proper name the chart uses, and the magnitude should match the catalogue value used to size the star.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > reset to zenith at ~18:38Z from 40N/105W > click the bright star labelled Capella.
location_wrong: object_info_popup.dart is where the heading renders (:343, `obj.name`) but nothing there is wrong - it faithfully shows the object it was handed. The fixable defect is upstream: the duplicate-row hit test and the name fallback at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/star_catalog.dart:236-253. Sending a fixer to object_info_popup.dart alone would not close it.
proposed_fix: Resolve the proper name (and its magnitude) from the same record the renderer labels from.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Searched 'Capella' - the result list shows 'Capella / Star - Aur / mag 0.1'; flying there, the chart draws the label 'Capella'; clicking the drawn star opens a popup headed 'HYG118360' with chip 'HYG118360', 'mag 1.0', 'Type: Star (G0 III)', RA 5h16m40.7s / Dec +45 59' 52" (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-28.png). I then found the cause in the installed catalog itself: hyg_v42.csv has TWO rows at that position - id 24549 (hip 24608, proper 'Capella', mag 0.08) and id 118360 (no hip, no proper name, mag 0.96, spect 'G0 III' - the Capella Ab component ~10 arcsec away). The hit test lands on the unnamed companion and star_catalog.dart:251-253 falls back to the raw id when proper/Bayer/Flamsteed are empty, so the popup names it 'HYG118360' and reports the companion's magnitude.

title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the night after tomorrow - every time is ~8 minutes wrong
what_happened: On 2026-08-02 at 40N/105W the Tonight sidebar listed IC311 with transit 09:24 and NGC6685 with transit 00:48. Selecting each object shows its coordinates in the bottom bar: IC311 = RA 3h16m46s Dec +40d00', NGC6685 = RA 18h39m58s Dec +39d58'. The true meridian crossings for those coordinates at lon -105 are 09:32 / 00:57 tonight (2026-08-02) and 09:28 / 00:53 the next night. The app's numbers match neither - they match 2026-08-04 (09:24 / 00:49), i.e. two sidereal days of drift. Root cause: bestTargetsProvider passes imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk as the 'date', and at this site astronomical dusk falls at 00:00-00:02 LOCAL, so its calendar day is already tomorrow; calculateObjectVisibility then builds its search window as DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12) + 24h, i.e. noon TOMORROW to noon the day after. Whether the list slips a day therefore depends on whether dusk lands before or after local midnight, which flips with longitude-within-timezone, DST and season - so the same code is right in winter and a day out in summer. The app also contradicts itself on the same screen: with NGC6685 selected, the sidebar's Info tab reports 'Transit 00:52' for the very object whose Best-Targets card two tabs away says 00:48.
expected: The visibility window for 'tonight' should start at the local noon preceding the dusk being planned for (or simply take a night-start date, not a dusk timestamp). Transit for IC311 tonight is 09:32, not 09:24.
repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > open the right sidebar > Tonight tab > scroll to 'Best Targets Tonight'. Note the transit time of a row, then click the row and read 'Center RA/Dec' in the bottom bar; compute the meridian crossing for that RA at that longitude.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-14.png (IC311 90 deg 09:24, NGC5311 19:58, NGC5313 19:59, IC4155 19:13, NGC6685 00:48), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-15.png (IC311 selected: Center RA 3h16m46s, Center Dec +40 00'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-16.png (NGC6685 selected: Center RA 18h39m58s, Center Dec +39 58'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:145-159 and astronomy_calculations.dart:1024-1025. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-17.png (Info tab for NGC6685: Transit 00:52) against rp2-14.png (Best Targets card for NGC6685: 00:48).
location_wrong: mosaic_targets.dart:146 is right for the caller. The other half a fixer must see is packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 (the localNoon/+24h window).
proposed_fix: Pass currentDate (the night's date) rather than the dusk instant, or have calculateObjectVisibility anchor its window on the noon BEFORE the supplied instant (subtract 12h before truncating to the day).
verdict_reasoning: The day-slip is real and I reproduced it deliberately, but the stated magnitude is wrong. Code unchanged: mosaic_targets.dart:145-149 passes imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk as the visibility `date`, and astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 builds the window as DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12) + 24 h, so whenever dusk lands after local midnight the window is the NEXT night. On today's date (2026-08-03) astro dusk shows 23:58, still calendar day Aug 3, and the list is CORRECT: IC311 09:24 and NGC6685 00:48 match my own transit computation for the Aug-3-noon window (13:24:15 and 04:48:52 UTC). I then set the planetarium date to Aug 2, 2026: astro dusk moves to 00:00 (calendar day Aug 3) and Best Targets STILL reports 09:24 / 00:48, whereas the correct values for the night of Aug 2 are 09:28 / 00:52 by my computation. That is the bug, reproduced. CORRECTION: the slip is ONE night, ~4 minutes, not 'the night after tomorrow' / '~8 minutes'. Severity lowered to P3 - a 4-minute transit error does not change which target you pick, and it only bites on nights where dusk crosses midnight.

title: After picking a search result the list silently re-runs on the object's name while the box still shows the typed query
what_happened: Typed '6720' in the plan panel's search field. The panel showed a '175 results' header with sections 'Deep Sky Objects (6)' = M57, NGC7107, IC728, NGC7112, IC5118, IC59 and 'Stars (169)'. Clicking the M57 row correctly recentred the chart on M57, but the result list underneath then changed to M57, M7, M47, 57 Cygnus, 57 Gemini, 57 Pegasus, 57 Virgo, 57 Ursa Major - matches for 'M57', not for '6720' - and the count header and the section headers disappeared. The text field still reads '6720'. The state is stable, not a transient: it still showed the same mismatch 90 seconds later.
expected: Either leave the result list exactly as typed (so the user can pick a second object from the same search), or clear the field when the query is replaced. Showing results for a query the box does not contain means 'back' from a wrong pick lands the user in a list they never asked for.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > right panel > Search tab > click the field > type '6720' > click the M57 row > look at the field and the list.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-32.png (query '6720': 175 results, Deep Sky Objects (6) = M57, NGC7107, IC728, NGC7112, IC5118, IC59), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-33.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-35.png (query still '6720', list is now M57, M7, M47, 57 Cygnus, 57 Gemini, 57 Pegasus, 57 Virgo, 57 Ursa Major).
location_wrong: Cited widgets/mobile_widgets/search_sheet.dart - that is the PHONE sheet and is not mounted on this desktop layout. The reproduced surface and the offending line are packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/search_header.dart:399-405, specifically `widget.onSearch(dso.name);` at :402.
proposed_fix: Do not push the selected object's name back into the search query on selection; if the intent is to show 'related objects', label it as such instead of leaving it looking like the result of the typed query.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Typed '6720' -> '175 results', 'Deep Sky Objects (6)' = M57, NGC7107, IC728, NGC7112, IC5118, IC59 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-15.png). Clicked the M57 row -> the chart correctly recentred (Center RA 18h53m35s / Dec +33 01') but the list became M57, M7, M47, 57 Cygnus, 57 Gemini, 57 Pegasus, 57 Virgo, 57 Ursa Major, the '175 results' count and section headers vanished, and the field still reads '6720' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-16.png). Root cause: the DSO result onTap calls widget.onSearch(dso.name) alongside selectObject/flyTo, re-running the query as 'M57' without touching the controller.

title: The Alt/Az view toggle throws away where you were looking and jumps the chart to the zenith
what_happened: With the chart centred on M57 at a 2.0 deg imaging FOV (Center RA 18h53m35s, Center Dec +33d 01'), clicking the command bar's second icon - tooltip 'Alt/Az view - tap for Equatorial' - immediately recentred the chart on RA 4h42m52s / Dec +39d 59'. At the LST shown in the status bar (04:43) that is exactly the zenith: hour angle 0, declination equal to the site latitude of 40 deg. The framing on M57 was gone, at 2 deg FOV, with no undo. Clicking the toggle back to Equatorial restored RA 18h53m35s / +33d 01', and toggling to Alt/Az a second time again landed on the zenith (RA 4h43m52s / +39d 59' at LST 04:44), so it is deterministic, not a transient.
expected: Changing the coordinate frame is a change of grid, not a change of target. The same patch of sky should stay under the cursor, just with the horizon-aligned grid and the up-vector rotated - that is what Stellarium and SkySafari do. If the app genuinely cannot express the current centre in the alt/az frame (e.g. the target is below the horizon) it should say so rather than silently slewing the view.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > centre on any object and zoom to a narrow FOV > click the second command bar icon ('Alt/Az view'). Read Center RA / Center Dec in the bottom bar and compare with the LST in the status bar and the site latitude.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-37.png (before: Center RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33 01', FOV 2.0), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-40.png (immediately after the toggle: Center RA 4h42m52s, Dec +39 59', tooltip 'Alt/Az view - tap for Equatorial', LST 04:43 in the status bar), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-41.png (toggled back: 18h53m35s / +33 01'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-42.png (toggled again: 4h43m52s / +39 59' at LST 04:44).
location_wrong: Cited command_bar.dart with no line. The handler is command_bar.dart:86-95 (duplicate at :384), but the behaviour a fixer must change is in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/sky_view.dart:33-36 (setViewMode) and :39-47 (setHorizontalCenter) - editing command_bar.dart alone cannot fix it.
proposed_fix: On frame change, convert the current centre RA/Dec to alt/az (and back) instead of resetting the centre to the zenith.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. With the chart on M57 (Center RA 18h53m35s / Dec +33 01', FOV 21.9), clicking the command bar's second icon jumped the centre to RA 10h37m46s / Dec +39 59' at LST ~10:37 - hour angle 0, dec = the 40 deg site latitude, i.e. the zenith (v2p-17.png). Toggling back restored 18h53m35s / +33 01' exactly (v2p-18.png). Mechanism: SkyViewNotifier.setViewMode (sky_view.dart:33-36) only flips viewMode; the horizontal frame keeps its own centerAz/centerAltitude, last set to (0,90) by _resetView (actions.dart:656). SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to P3: the finding's own evidence shows one click restores the pose exactly, contradicting its 'with no undo' framing.

title: The app states three different, all-wrong depths for the bundled star catalog: 'mag <= 15.0', '~mag 11.5' and 'below mag 11.5 unavailable'
what_happened: Reached from the planetarium's Layers panel > Deep stars > Install, the Catalog Settings sheet describes the installed HYG Star Database as '119.6k objects, 32.4 MB, Version 4.2, Package Complete, Depth mag <= 15.0'. Two cards further down, the Deep-Star Tier card says the same bundled catalog's floor is '~mag 11.5'. The Layers panel itself says 'stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable'. All three are wrong in the same direction: 119,600 stars spread over 41,253 square degrees is 2.9 stars per square degree, and that is exactly the density I measured on screen (about 25 stars in a 3.8 x 2.0 deg field at FOV 2.0). A catalog complete to mag 15 would contain tens of millions of stars; HYG (Hipparcos + Yale BSC + Gliese) is complete to roughly magnitude 9. 'Package: Complete' next to 'Depth: mag <= 15.0' tells the user the empty field they are looking at is the real sky.
expected: State the completeness limit, not the faintest entry: about mag 9 for HYG. And make the three surfaces agree.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > command bar Layers icon > 'Deep stars (Tycho-2 / Gaia tier)' > Install > read the HYG card, then scroll to the Deep-Star Tier card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-51.png (HYG card: Objects 119.6k, Package Complete, Depth mag <= 15.0), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-56.png (Deep-Star Tier card: 'below the bundled HYG floor (~mag 11.5)'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-43.png (Layers panel: 'No tileset installed - stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-37.png (the measured field at FOV 2.0).
location_wrong: Cited deep_star_providers.dart:25 - that constant is already corrected to 9.0 and is now the only right number in the app. The surviving wrong strings are packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/deep_star_catalog_card.dart:225 ('~mag 11.5') and the descriptor fed by packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/star_catalog.dart:29 (magnitudeLimit = 15.0).
proposed_fix: One constant for HYG's completeness (~9.0), used by the Layers subtitle, the Catalog Settings depth chip and the deep-star merge seam.
verdict_reasoning: Still three disagreeing numbers, though not the three named. Read live from the running app's accessibility tree in Catalog Settings (reached via Layers > Deep stars > Install): the HYG Star Database card still shows 'Depth: mag <= 15.0'; the Deep-Star Tier card still reads 'Streams faint stars below the bundled HYG floor (~mag 11.5)'; the Layers panel has since been corrected to 'stars below mag 9.0 are unavailable'. So two of the three survive verbatim and now contradict the fixed third. I verified the true depth myself from hyg_v42.csv: 119,626 rows, per-magnitude gain turns over after 9 (25,690 in 7-8, 41,975 in 8-9, 24,814 in 9-10, 7,580 in 10-11) - 15.0 and 11.5 are both wrong, 9.0 is right. 'mag <= 15.0' is actually the loader's filter, HygStarCatalog(magnitudeLimit: 15.0), mislabelled 'Depth'. Severity lowered to P3: with the layers panel corrected this is stale copy on two settings cards, not the load-bearing seam it was.

title: 'Install' on the deep-star tier leads to a form asking the user to build and self-host a tileset - no tileset exists to install
what_happened: The Layers panel row 'Deep stars (Tycho-2 / Gaia tier)' carries a button labelled 'Install'. Pressing it opens Catalog Settings; scrolling to the matching card reveals 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)' with an empty 'Tileset base URL' text field, a Download button, and the line 'No official tileset is published yet - point this at a tileset you host yourself (see tools/catalog_prep in the Skotiq repository).' So the button named Install cannot install anything: the user is expected to clone the repo, run a catalog-preparation tool, and stand up a web server. Meanwhile the same row is what the app blames for the empty sky at imaging FOVs.
expected: Either publish and host the tileset (the DSS survey layer already proves the app can fetch remote sky data), or stop calling the button 'Install' - label it 'Configure source...' and say up front that no public tileset exists. As shipped this is the single biggest gap between what the planetarium claims and what it can draw.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > Layers > Install (on the Deep stars row) > scroll Catalog Settings to 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-43.png (the Install button), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-56.png (the card it leads to, with the empty Tileset base URL field and the 'No official tileset is published yet' note).
location_wrong: deep_star_catalog_card.dart is right for the form and the 'no official tileset' copy, but the mislabelled button lives in a different file: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/layers_panel.dart:442-447.
proposed_fix: Ship a hosted Tycho-2 tileset (a catalogs-vN GitHub release already exists for the other catalogs) or relabel the button and the layer subtitle to match reality.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. The Layers panel row still carries a button labelled 'Install' (layers_panel.dart:442-447, seen live in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-24.png); pressing it opens Catalog Settings whose 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)' card exposes an empty 'Tileset base URL' field and the line 'No official tileset is published yet - point this at a tileset you host yourself (see tools/catalog_prep in the Skotiq repository).' - both read straight off the running app's accessibility tree. So the control named Install cannot install anything. Severity lowered to P3: the substantive half ('publish and host the tileset') is a product/infrastructure decision, not a code defect; the closable defect is the misleading button label plus the copy.

title: Your Sky says '1 region imaged' for a region that has zero frames, zero tiles and zero seconds of integration
what_happened: On a fresh profile with no captures at all, I used Your Sky > Name a region > Custom RA/Dec (RA 283.4, Dec 33.03, radius 0.5, name 'Ring Region'). The Regions header immediately read '1 region imaged'. Directly above it the Atlas coverage strip correctly reads 0s Integration / 0 Tiles / 0 Frames, and the region card itself reads '0s' and '0 tiles'. Naming a patch of sky is not imaging it, and the screen's own numbers say so.
expected: '1 region' (or '1 region, none imaged yet'). The count should say what it counts; 'imaged' is a claim about captured data that the same screen contradicts twice.
repro: Plan Tonight > Discover > Your Sky > Name a region > Custom RA/Dec > RA 283.4, Dec 33.03, name anything > Create region. Read the Regions header against the Atlas coverage tiles.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-77.png ('Atlas coverage 0s / 0 / 0' above 'Regions - 1 region imaged' above a card reading 'Ring Region  18h 54m . +33 02'  0s  0 tiles').
proposed_fix: Pluralise on the region count alone, and only say 'imaged' for regions with frames > 0.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh profile with no captures. Plan Tonight > Discover > Your Sky > Name a region > Custom RA/Dec (RA 283.4, Dec 33.03, radius 0.5, 'Ring Region'). The screen then reads 'Regions / 1 region imaged' directly above a card 'Ring Region  18h 54m . +33 02'  0s  0 tiles', with the Atlas coverage strip reading 0s Integration / 0 Frames (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-34.png). I confirmed the emptiness in the DB rather than trusting the UI: sky_atlas_regions = 1, sky_tiles = 0, sky_atlas_folds = 0, captured_images = 0. The string is at the cited file, your_sky_screen.dart:133 - location exact.

title: 'Name a region' keeps showing the validation error 'Pick a target first.' after you switch to the Custom RA/Dec mode that has no target to pick
what_happened: In Your Sky > Name a region the 'From a target' mode says 'No targets in your library yet - switch to Custom to enter a sky position by hand', yet Create region is enabled; pressing it produces the red error 'Pick a target first.'. Switching to the Custom RA/Dec mode as instructed leaves that error on screen, and it stays there while you fill in RA 283.4, Dec 33.03 and a name - i.e. the dialog is telling the user to do something the current mode does not offer, right up to the moment the region is created successfully.
expected: Clear the validation message when the mode changes or any field is edited, and disable Create region while the form cannot be submitted (rather than enabling it and explaining afterwards).
repro: Plan Tonight > Discover > Your Sky > Name a region > Create region (error appears) > switch to 'Custom RA/Dec' > fill RA/Dec/name. The error is still displayed.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-74.png (error in 'From a target' mode), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-75.png (still shown after switching to Custom RA/Dec), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-76.png (still shown with RA 283.4, Dec 33.03 and 'Ring Region' filled in).
location_wrong: Cited packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/your_sky/your_sky_screen.dart. The sheet is a different file: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/your_sky/widgets/name_region_sheet.dart - mode switch that fails to clear at :99, error render at :114-117, message at :281.
proposed_fix: Reset the error string in the mode-switch and field-change handlers.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced step for step. In 'From a target' mode the sheet says 'No targets in your library yet - switch to Custom to enter a sky position by hand' yet Create region is fully enabled (v2p-31.png); pressing it produces the red 'Pick a target first.'. Switching to 'Custom RA/Dec' leaves that error on screen (v2p-32.png), and it is STILL displayed after filling RA 283.4, Dec 33.03 and the name 'Ring Region' (v2p-33.png), right up to a successful create. Code matches: _error is only assigned inside _create (:281, :307, :336, :347) and cleared at :267 on the next submit; the mode radio at :99 is `onChanged: (s) => setState(() => _source = s)` with no _error reset, and no text field clears it.
